purpose: Reproducibility check for the post-bugfix 3.861x speedup number, requested by the user before trusting it -- reruns the same benchmark with a different random seed batch (BASE_SEED changed from 400 to 900).
interpretation: The cached path is highly stable across both seed batches (~14.7-15.4s mean, ~1s std). The no-cache path is noisy (~18-19s std, ~30% of its mean) -- consistent with the earlier MPS per-call dispatch overhead / system-noise hypothesis, since no-cache does fewer, larger forward passes where system jitter shows up more in the total. Every individual per-run ratio across both seed batches is >=3.5x; the speedup point estimate moves (3.861x vs 4.400x) because the noisy no-cache baseline moves, but the qualitative conclusion ('cached is at least ~3.5x faster, not a one-off result') is reproduced under an independent seed batch.
